edges.mechanism: Phenelzine (Nardil) US label lists L-tyrosine among 'related compounds' (with L-dopa, L-tryptophan, phenylalanine) that patients should not take because of hypertensive-crisis risk. Tyrosine is a catecholamine precursor, not tyramine: the classic MAOI dietary pressor reaction is caused by tyramine (a decarboxylated amine normally cleared by gut/hepatic MAO), so tyramine-diet data cannot be transferred to tyrosine.
edges.evidence: Label warning only (phenelzine; not in tranylcypromine label); no published tyrosine-MAOI hypertensive-crisis case found; the only review asserting safety (Hinz 2014) is retracted

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine is a large neutral amino acid competing with levodopa for intestinal transport and for LAT1 (SLC7A5) at the blood-brain barrier; oral LNAAs (100 mg/kg) reversed infused levodopa's clinical effect without lowering plasma levodopa. Separate tyrosine from levodopa doses.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic + human LNAA challenge study (tyrosine itself not tested) + label high-protein warning; 7-day RCT of 1 g/d tyrosine in levodopa-treated PD showed no harm

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine availability scales amphetamine-evoked dopamine release: acute tyrosine/phenylalanine depletion reduced d-amphetamine-induced striatal DA release (PET) and subjective stimulant effects. Loading could plausibly augment stimulant effects (additive catecholaminergic action); phenelzine label also groups amphetamines with tyrosine.
edges.evidence: Human depletion studies (converse direction); no human loading + amphetamine study

edges.mechanism: Exogenous tyrosine potentiated and prolonged methylphenidate-induced extracellular dopamine in rat nucleus accumbens.
edges.evidence: Animal microdialysis only

edges.mechanism: Nitisinone (NTBC) blocks HPPD and raises plasma tyrosine; hypertyrosinemia causes keratopathy (symptoms controlled below ~600 umol/L); management is tyrosine/phenylalanine restriction, so supplemental tyrosine is counterproductive.
edges.evidence: Case reports, case series and observational dietary studies in alkaptonuria

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine is the backbone of T4/T3, but hormones are formed by TPO iodination of tyrosyl residues within thyroglobulin under TSH control; free tyrosine is not rate-limiting. No interaction expected; no study found.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic; 12-month tyrosine use in YARS2 disease showed no thyroid toxicity

edges.mechanism: Theoretical concern because tyrosine is a thyroid-hormone and catecholamine precursor; physiologically, iodide and TSH, not tyrosine, drive synthesis. A catecholamine precursor could theoretically add to adrenergic symptoms (HR/BP rose during a multitask battery in a 150 mg/kg trial, not clearly attributable to tyrosine).
edges.evidence: Mechanistic only; no clinical data in hyperthyroid patients

edges.mechanism: Complementary substrates of thyroid hormone synthesis (iodide is oxidized by TPO and incorporated into thyroglobulin tyrosyl residues); iodine availability is the nutritional limit, so no additive thyroid effect from co-supplementation is expected.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic reviews; no co-supplementation study

edges.mechanism: Complementary mechanisms (adenosine antagonism + catecholamine precursor); commonly co-formulated. A caffeine+theanine+tyrosine product improved movement accuracy in athletes; caffeine and tyrosine are the leading military nootropic candidates, though caffeine drives most energy-drink effects.
edges.evidence: One industry-funded crossover RCT of a combination product (n=20); expert reviews; contribution of tyrosine not isolated

edges.mechanism: Often combined for 'calm focus'. In a 3-arm RCT (n=80) neither altered salivary stress markers; only tyrosine 2 g reduced Stroop missed responses. Combination only tested within a caffeine-containing product.
edges.evidence: RCT comparing each alone; one combination-product RCT; synergy unproven

edges.mechanism: In bipolar disorder, dietary tyrosine depletion reduced mania ratings, implying tyrosine loading could work against antimanic treatment; lithium (unlike clozapine) did not correct reduced fibroblast tyrosine uptake in bipolar patients.
edges.evidence: Small RCT of depletion in mania (n=20); in vitro fibroblast study; no tyrosine-loading data

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine-free amino acid mixture attenuated methamphetamine effects and lowered mania ratings, supporting a role of precursor availability in pathological dopamine overactivity; supplementation during mania is theoretically counterproductive.
edges.evidence: Small randomized study; inference by converse mechanism

edges.mechanism: Defective tyrosine catabolism (FAH, TAT, HPD); management requires lifelong tyrosine/phenylalanine restriction; elevated tyrosine causes corneal and palmoplantar lesions and neurocognitive effects.
edges.evidence: Consensus guideline, GeneReviews, StatPearls

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine is conditionally essential and already supplied in Phe-free protein substitutes; extra free tyrosine raised blood tyrosine without improving cognition and causes large diurnal swings, possibly unsafe for the fetus in maternal PKU. Specialist-directed only.
edges.evidence: Cochrane SR (3 RCTs, n=56); crossover RCTs; expert review

edges.mechanism: Older adults reach higher plasma tyrosine per mg/kg; higher doses (100-200 mg/kg) worsened load-dependent working memory and, with increasing age, proactive response inhibition and fronto-striatal signal (inverted-U dopamine response).
edges.evidence: Two small randomized crossover studies (n=17, n=24)

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine is the melanogenesis substrate and a hormone-like regulator of melanocytes; high tyrosine drove primary melanoma cultures toward invasive, MAPK-inhibitor-resistant phenotypes. Human Tyr/Phe-restricted diets showed no tumor response.
edges.evidence: In vitro and rodent data; small human diet studies; no data on supplementation and melanoma outcomes

edges.mechanism: Cirrhosis raises endogenous tyrosine appearance and plasma aromatic amino acids; a low BCAA:aromatic (Fischer) ratio tracks hepatic encephalopathy grade, so adding aromatic amino acid is undesirable.
edges.evidence: Isotope kinetic study; review; no supplementation study

edges.with: plasma amino acid profile (tyrosine, Phe:Tyr ratio)
edges.mechanism: Supplementation raises plasma tyrosine (about 2-fold 2 h after 2.5 g; modest fasting rise at 4 g/d) and Tyr:LNAA ratios, which can confound interpretation of plasma amino acids and Phe:Tyr monitoring in PKU.
edges.evidence: RCT pharmacokinetic data; PKU practice survey

edges.mechanism: Newborn screening for HT-1 relies on succinylacetone, which is more specific than tyrosine; tyrosine and Tyr/Phe are adjunct markers (PPV rose from 9% to 72%) and elevated tyrosine flags type II. Exogenous tyrosine could raise tyrosine-based markers; succinylacetone is unaffected by precursor intake (inference).
edges.evidence: Systematic review of test accuracy; consensus guideline; national screening evaluation

edges.mechanism: Tyrosine 100 mg/kg/d increased urinary MHPG; 6.5 g raised plasma norepinephrine, epinephrine and dopamine under heat stress. May shift biochemical catecholamine testing; no assay study found.
edges.evidence: RCT secondary outcomes

edges.mechanism: T/T homozygotes (presumed lower striatal dopamine) showed larger tyrosine benefits on stop-signal and N-back performance than C/C.
edges.evidence: Single RCT from one laboratory
